newsitem.title: USA: Reno says Cunanan case to be reviewed.
newsitem.headline: Reno says Cunanan case to be reviewed.

text.p: The case of Andrew Cunanan, suspected of killing fashion designer Gianni Versace and four other men, will be reviewed to determine what might have been handled differently, Attorney General Janet Reno said Thursday.
Cunanan, who had been the subject of a nationwide FBI manhunt, was found on a houseboat in Miami Beach early on Thursday, apparently having committed suicide.

"What we always do is try to look at what was done to see, as Monday morning quarterbacks, what we might have done differently. I think it is important in any instance like this to look at processes and procedures," Reno said.
"We always want to take steps to see that we've done everything that we can. And in this instance, I think we will do it again," she said at her weekly Justice Department news briefing.
Reno's comments came in response to questions about allegations that the FBI and local police had missed a number of opportunities to apprehend Cunanan.
She said the FBI had been vigorously pursuing Cunanan before Versace's murder last week, noting that he had been placed in June on the FBI's list of 10 most wanted fugitives.
"I think there is a frustration...when a tragedy like this (Versace's murder) occurs, and you're constantly thinking what could have been done to have prevented it," Reno said.
"What lead might I have followed? What might I have done? And it is important that if we can learn anything from that, we do so," she said.
